idiom_name: axum Json/Html response types + askama template structs over one model
implementation_notes: There is no view resolver to configure: the model is a serde-serializable struct, each representation is its own response type - axum::Json for application/json, axum::response::Html built from an askama-rendered template, a CSV writer or a PDF crate - and negotiation is the handler's own match on the Accept header returning impl IntoResponse or Response. Askama derives Template on the context struct so the HTML view is type-checked against the model at compile time, which is the idiomatic substitute for a shared presentation model. A registry of renderers behind a trait object is only worth the extra plumbing in a plugin host that must load renderers at run time.
pitfalls: Deriving both Serialize and Template on one struct welds the domain type to every representation; split into a domain struct plus per-view projection structs instead of accumulating derives.
render() returns Result: unwrapping it in a handler turns a template bug into a panic that aborts the task, so map it to a 500 response.
Askama compiles templates into the binary (rebuild to change markup) while tera loads them at run time; choosing the wrong one surprises either the dev loop or the deployment story.
